perf_defaults.note: Legacy evaluation-policy-v1 defaults, retained only for the experimental conv task. The judge-level perf_phase_budget_seconds is likewise legacy-only. The nine scored Stage 1 problems define independent grouped cases in problems/<id>/config.json, and their evaluation-policy-v2 cohorts seal perf_phase_budget_seconds=0 so one case cannot consume another case's configured time allowance. Official evaluation requires a hidden PERF_SEED and seals the resolved schedule into the cohort policy; an unseeded schedule is for deterministic local development only.

timing.note: Local dev uses wall_time. Stage 1 official cohorts use in-container local-v2 perf_instructions on the pinned Linux PMU host. KTP/3 is non-official validation only. Metrics are ranked separately. Correctness and target declarations use three replays and record each median. Process startup, export parsing, and per-input dependency preload are excluded; exact output-literal checking remains included. KTP/3 binds each remote target replay to the published memory limit and reports memory exhaustion during that replay as a case resource-limit outcome. Memory exhaustion during timed correctness replay leaves an otherwise accepted submission unscored. Other protocol or boundary versions are legacy/unscored.

scoring.contract: nine independent problem leaderboards; group_points_desc, then ordered-case profile or interchangeable-case counts, then the eligible configured work/proof tie-break
scoring.policy_source: problems/<id>/config.json evaluation (grouped-evaluation-v1), sealed into each evaluation-policy-v2 cohort
scoring.note: There is no cross-problem total. Each scored problem publishes its three groups, hidden-case count, milestones, resource limits, and proof/work tie-break. All work terms must use the verdict's one metric, protocol, measurement contract, boundary versions, and target-proof encoding. Alpha and beta never affect rank. Rankings never cross problem, metric, cohort, or measurement version.

sandbox.note: 'none' = local dev via the landrun pass-through shim (NO sandboxing). 'container' asserts a real landrun is present and is set by the Docker image. Resource/isolation limits (memory, cpus, pids, network, non-root, kill-all-on-exit) are ENFORCED BY scripts/run_isolated.sh and the container runtime, not by the judge process.
